reason: Ten confirmed audit findings remain: five recorder-glibc semantic/resource defects, three discriminating test gaps, and two evaluator-contract comments. The matcher must reach source parity and bounded resource behavior before this slice is ready for audit.

boundary.startingEvent: A valid ASCII POSIX ERE from startup MSGTYPE or AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION is compiled, diagnosed, and matched through the recorder-glibc wrapper contract.
boundary.endingEvent: Compilation returns the recorder diagnostic or installed matching selects the same boolean/action as glibc within a documented polynomial resource budget through the source 255-byte pattern and message limits.
boundary.validInputs: Recorder-glibc REG_EXTENDED|REG_NOSUB ASCII patterns with alternatives, groups, numeric references, contextual and GNU anchors, classes, exact/open/bounded intervals, malformed unterminated intervals, empty matches, and ambiguous repetition.
boundary.observables: Compile acceptance and exact diagnostic category, match boolean and selected MSGTYPE action, installed startup state, complete screens/cursors and PRNG calls, plus wall-time and memory/state-count bounds for adversarial valid patterns.
boundary.exclusions: Non-ASCII C.UTF-8 locale collation/classes, runtime autopickup object filtering, interactive MSGTYPE editing/serialization, USER_SOUNDS, and behavior after the next message/input boundary remain named before-effect boundaries.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: sys/share/posixregex.c regex_init/regex_match delegates to recorder glibc regcomp/regexec; options.c msgtype_parse_add/msgtype_type and add_autopickup_exception are the live startup consumers.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: The complete ASCII ERE grammar, capture/reference ids, repetition bounds through RE_DUP_MAX, anchor position rules, and MSGTYPE/AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION pattern storage define the families.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: The expanded correctness audit supplied direct glibc discriminators for every semantic defect and adversarial valid patterns for both resource defects; related AST arms and compile diagnostics were clustered by shared ownership.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: Inspect js/posixregex.js regex_compile/regex_match, parser/translator/evaluator helpers, js/options.js consumers, and the focused/direct/fresh regex runners for duplicated engines, unsupported fallbacks, and V8 RegExp routing.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The audit is exhaustive for the ten recorded deferrals. The worker must still trace glibc leftmost/longest and subgroup precedence closely enough to replace enumeration without overfitting the listed examples.

entries.reachability: A reference follows an ambiguous bounded or nested repetition with several mathematically valid decompositions.
entries.effects: The selected capture decomposition determines whether the reference matches and which startup rule applies.
entries.evidence: Audit probes reject ^(a){0,2}\1$ on aa, ^(a){1,3}\1$ on aaa, ^(a+)+\1$ on aaa, and unanchored (l){0,2}\1 on Hello while the current evaluator accepts them.
entries.remaining: Implemented with glibc-shaped interval endpoint and nested quantified-capture selection; focused and direct libc cases pass.

entries.reachability: A zero-width prefix reaches an internal caret immediately after a newline that the current candidate did not consume.
entries.owner: js/posixregex.js direct and reference-aware anchor evaluation
entries.effects: The current code admits matches glibc rejects in both matcher representations.
entries.evidence: glibc rejects ()^b on newline+b and (()^b)\1 on newline+bb; both accept the consumed-newline control .+^b.
entries.remaining: Both representations carry candidate-start provenance; direct/reference failures and the consumed-newline control pass against libc.

entries.reachability: A brace expression has invalid comma-form content and no closing brace.
entries.effects: Startup configuration reports the wrong libc diagnostic text/category.
entries.evidence: Fresh recorder-libc probes report Invalid content of braces for `(a)\1{a,`, `a{a,,`, `a{a,`, and `a{1a,`, but Unmatched brace for `a{,`, `a{1,`, `a{a`, and `a{1`.
entries.remaining: Unterminated comma-form scanning follows parse_dup_op() diagnostic precedence; reference and direct controls pass against libc.

entries.candidate: Polynomial resource bound for reference-aware matching
entries.reachability: A short valid nested ambiguous pattern with references creates many capture-range states.
entries.effects: Synchronous startup or message matching can take seconds and allocate hundreds of MiB.
entries.evidence: The audit measured a 25-byte valid nested pattern on 16 bytes at about 6.2 seconds/108 MiB versus glibc about 0.01 seconds/2 MiB; larger prior probes reached hundreds of MiB.
entries.remaining: The evaluator retains immutable values only for referenced groups; the 255-byte-pattern/255-byte-input adversary passes the 2,000 ms/128 MiB maxRSS budget without an abort.

entries.candidate: Polynomial resource bound for no-reference matching
entries.reachability: A valid ambiguous no-reference pattern is routed to native V8 RegExp on a BUFSZ-scale nonmatch.
entries.effects: Native exponential backtracking can stall every ordinary vpline consumer.
entries.evidence: ^(a|aa)*b$ on 40 a bytes took about 13 seconds in JavaScript while recorder glibc rejected 255 bytes in under 0.01 seconds.
entries.remaining: The direct path uses memoized Thompson position sets; the 255-byte-pattern/255-byte-input adversary passes the 1,000 ms/96 MiB maxRSS budget and libc result.

entries.candidate: Reference-aware class and anchor arm coverage
entries.reachability: Numeric-reference patterns also contain POSIX classes, GNU absolute anchors, or contextual anchors.
entries.effects: AST-only parser/evaluator arms can regress while no-reference tests stay green.
entries.evidence: Existing semantic cases for these constructs route to the direct matcher; the audit exposed an AST anchor defect this gap concealed.
entries.remaining: Focused and direct-libc cases cover reference-aware POSIX class, GNU buffer anchors, and internal caret while asserting the representation.

entries.reachability: A capture repetition permits more than one bounded count before a reference.
entries.effects: Treating {m,n} as exact or open would escape current tests.
entries.evidence: The missing matrix for ^(a){2,3}\1$ rejects aa/aaaaa and matches aaa/aaaa in recorder glibc.
entries.remaining: The four-input ^(a){2,3}\1$ matrix passes focused and direct-libc validation.

entries.candidate: Variable-width capture overwrite and retention coverage
entries.reachability: A subgroup changes width when participating and is then retained through nonparticipating siblings.
entries.effects: Stale start/end or fixed-width capture bugs can pass all existing equal-width tests.
entries.evidence: Audit glibc probes for ^((ab|c)|x)*\2$ distinguish overwrite, retention, content, and span length.
entries.remaining: The ^((ab|c)|x)*\2$ overwrite/retention matrix passes focused and direct-libc validation.

entries.candidate: Capture-state key completeness and immutability contract
entries.reachability: State deduplication assumes position plus every capture range fully determines future behavior.
entries.effects: A future mutable or unkeyed field could merge unequal paths or corrupt stored alternatives.
entries.evidence: The audit confirmed the current invariant is necessary and correct but implicit at its definition.
entries.remaining: captureStateKey() documents immutability and complete future-equivalence for referenced values.

entries.reachability: An enclosing group participates through a sibling path where a descendant does not.
entries.effects: Conventional clearing would lose glibc's last participating descendant value.
entries.evidence: Existing equal-width cases prove retention, but the mechanism that overwrites only the enclosing span is not locally explained.
entries.remaining: The group transition documents why only the enclosing span changes and descendants retain their last participating values.

sourceReview: Complete. Traced sys/share/posixregex.c's REG_EXTENDED|REG_NOSUB wrapper, glibc regcomp.c parse_dup_op()/mark_opt_subexp(), regexec.c get_subexp()/capture-state paths, and the installed MSGTYPE/AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION consumers. Fresh libc probes settled bounded-repeat endpoints, nested quantified captures, internal-caret provenance, and malformed-interval diagnostic precedence.
